segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast, we have real conversations in easy English to help you understand.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. You can watch a video of this podcast and find a worksheet to help you learn on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Beth, how are you today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very good, Neil. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well. What are we talking about?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Today we are talking about work and the office.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: An office is a place with desks and computers where people do their jobs.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, we are in a studio in the office, but we'll go back to the office after this.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, we will. So, Neil, where do you work? Do you work at home or do you work in the office?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I do both of those things.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I work in the office usually three days a week and I work from home two days a week.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. I'm the same. We have the same schedule.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So yeah at home twice where I have a sort of place that could be considered a home office Do you like working in the office

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I do like working in the office I think it easy to get work done in the office because it an office environment It a workplace

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I also quite like working from home sometimes because commuting, London is a big city, you know,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: coming to work and going back is really tiring if you do it every day.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, I know what you mean. I like working from home occasionally, but I definitely prefer being in the office. I think being with colleagues around you and I need people and then I can work better.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. So what's wrong with working from home?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh, a lot. I think when you're in the office, yeah, it's louder than at home. But I like having the people around me. I like being able to have conversations. I find it's easier to work in an office environment because everyone else is working. But I feel more lonely at home because it's just me. So, yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah I understand what you mean I also have a bit of a problem with working from home because the boundary or the line between work and home is not so clear

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So when you finish your day, you close your computer and you think, oh, hang on, I'm still at home.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: This is where I've been working all day. And sometimes you feel like you should be doing things for home when you're actually working.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, it's a bit weirder. It's strange being at home because it's harder to know whether you should be working or doing a bit of housework. In the office, it's easier to just sit, be with your laptop, be with your colleagues and just be working.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Have you ever worked somewhere that is not an office?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, so I used to work at a farm

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It was a farm park, so lots of children playing

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And there was a cafe, there was a play area, go-karts, being with animals

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So lots of different areas and it was fun, lots of variety

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So that wasn't an office

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I've worked in all kinds of places, especially when I was a student

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I've worked in factories, farms.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I worked in restaurants bars all kinds of places that are not offices

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You done it all

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Done it all

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap some of the vocabulary we heard in this podcast.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We had office, a place with desks and computers where people go to work.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Sometimes at BBC Learning English we work in the office.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We had working remotely, which we often also call working from home.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And that means working somewhere that isn't the office.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, your home, but it could also be a cafe or something.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We also had colleagues. These are the people that you work with.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we compared working from home with working from an office.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we used lots of comparatives.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: so it's harder to concentrate at home

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or it's more difficult to get your work done in the office.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, and it's louder in the office, but sometimes that's better.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can test what you've learned with a worksheet,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: which you can download for free from our website,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And next time, we'll be talking all about games.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: See you then!

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye!
